precepts.text: Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow.
precepts.point: He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life as a child, and this one had beheaded John.

note.label: Luke 23: The Trial, the Crucifixion, and the Burial

precepts.why:
Herod “was exceeding glad” to see Jesus, hoping to see some miracle, and “questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.” He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life when he was a child, and this Herod had beheaded John.

He had already named what that man was. When the Pharisees came saying “Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee”, he answered, “Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.” Herod is a fox. Christ would not stop his work for him then, and he would not perform for him now. The cures and the casting out of devils were his work, not a show for Herod.

precepts.text: He is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament.
precepts.point: The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.

note.label: Luke 23: The Trial, the Crucifixion, and the Burial

precepts.why:
At the ninth hour the sun was darkened “and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.” The rending of the veil is a sign: what stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.

Hebrews gives the meaning. “How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” His blood does what the blood of the sacrifices did, and more.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” His death redeems the transgressions that were under the first testament. So when he gave up the ghost and the veil was torn, the offering had been made; the sacrifices of the first testament had come to their end and the new testament had its mediator.

precepts.text: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day.
precepts.point: The women returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment. That is written after the death, in the new testament.

note.label: Luke 23: The Trial, the Crucifixion, and the Burial

precepts.why:
Joseph of Arimathaea, “a good man, and a just”, who “had not consented to the counsel and deed of them”, went to Pilate and begged the body, took it down, wrapped it in linen and laid it in a sepulchre hewn in stone, all the same day, while “the sabbath drew on.”

He was buried the same day because that is the custom written in the law. “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled”. Christ was hanged on a tree, and a body hanged on a tree does not remain all night. There is no waiting days over a body.

Joseph did it according to the law, and the women who followed did the same: they prepared spices and ointments “and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.” That is written after the death, in the new testament. The law was kept at the burial of Christ, and the sabbath was kept after he died.

moments.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Behold, there was a man named Joseph, a counsellor; and he was a good man, and a just: the same had not consented to the counsel and deed of them. Not every man is allowed into the council of the Pharisees, so this scripture lets you know Joseph of Arimathaea had close relations with the Pharisees, but he was a follower of Christ.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Who also himself waited for the kingdom of God: he knew the kingdom of God was only going to come by the Messiah, Christ, and he accepted that. That's why he asked Pilate for the body of Christ.

These men had the fortitude to go against the grain, that evil movement of the Pharisees to destroy Christ and his followers, and say: what y'all doing is wrong; y'all persecuting these brothers wrongfully. And these are just the two that are mentioned; the Bible is written in an abbreviated form. We pray that same spirit falls on many of these Israelites out there who secretly see the evil in their own congregations and are biding their time until they also walk out those doors.
